standard_prerequisites: The situation of a map of quasi-coherent modules over the base with flat target, and the pullback of the map to the fibres over points of the base

Etale locality of the vanishing of the pullback of a module map on a fibre, and the existence of an etale neighbourhood on which the source becomes projective over the base with a prescribed point of the fibre covered
The ideal of a map between a module and a projective module, and the description of its vanishing locus as the set of points where the pulled back map is zero
core_obligations: Observe that the vanishing of the pullback of the map to the fibre over the given point is etale local on that fibre, and pass to an etale neighbourhood where the source becomes projective over the base with the point of the fibre still covered

Record that the image of the given set of points under the etale morphism still has the chosen point in its closure, because the etale morphism is open, and thereby reduce to the corresponding algebra statement

In the algebra statement, with the target projective over the ring and the pulled back map to the residue field of every point of the set equal to zero, introduce the ideal attached to the map, note that the set is contained in its vanishing locus and that the chosen point lies in the closure of the set, hence also in the vanishing locus, and conclude that the pulled back map at the chosen point is zero
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an etale neighbourhood where the source is projective over the base
Transfer the closure condition along the open etale morphism
Conclude in the algebra setting using the ideal of the map and its vanishing locus
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the propagation of the vanishing of a base changed map from a set of points to its closure at source lines 1647-1662, label lemma-F-zero-somewhat-closed-points, whose proof occupies source lines 1664-1689. The proof reduces the geometric statement to an algebra statement in two steps that both need care: the vanishing is checked etale locally on the fibre, so one passes to an etale neighbourhood on which the source becomes projective over the base while still covering the chosen point of the fibre, and the closure condition is preserved because an etale morphism is open, so the chosen point remains in the closure of the image of the set. The algebra statement is then settled with the ideal attached to the map and its vanishing locus. The counted statement records neither the etale neighbourhood nor the transfer of the closure condition.
